newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL GOV'T SELLS VIRTUALLY ALL COFFEE IN AUCTION.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL GOV'T SELLS VIRTUALLY ALL COFFEE IN AUCTION.

text.p: The Brazilian government sold 99.73 percent or 85,570 60-kg bags of the 85,800 bags of coffee stocks offered to all segments of the coffee sector in its auction today, according to a Banco do Brasil official.
Total revenue for the government was 13.54 million reais ($12.42 million).
Closing prices for arabica coffee were up to 30 reais higher than opening levels set by the government.
The one lot of robusta coffee was sold for 130.05 reais a bag, up 49.05 reais from the opening price of 81 reais.
"There was very little coffee on offer which is why the prices were so high," said Americo Sato, vice-president of the Brazilian Coffee Industry Association (Abic).

"Even though the new crop is coming in, roasters also need coffee from previous harvests to make blends. Today, older coffees hardly exist on the market, there is only the government stocks," he added.
